current_identifiers.result: Raw Jayapala caused mortality and severe gastrointestinal toxicity at 2000 mg/kg, whereas Shodhita Jayapala produced no mortality or toxicity, indicating successful detoxification by Shodhana.

No mortality was observed even at 2000 mg/kg over 14 days; only transiently decreased locomotor activity and slight body-weight/behavioral changes were observed at the highest dose, while 50 and 300 mg/kg produced no significant changes.
No mortality, behavioral abnormalities, or signs of toxicity were observed at 2000 mg/kg, with an LD₅₀ > 2000 mg/kg, indicating low acute toxicity.

HPTLC showed that Shodhana with tamarind leaf juice altered the phytochemical profile of E. caducifolia latex, with increased lupeol (chosen as a marker for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity) levels in shade-dried samples as juice concentration increased.
HPTLC showed gradual degradation of toxic di-ester alkaloids with decreased aconitine and increased mono-ester alkaloids in Vatsanabha after shodhana.

HPTLC showed a strong aconitine band at Rf 0.21 in raw Vatsanabha (peak area 1541.7 AU), which markedly decreased after Shodhana (257.5 AU) with appearance of new peaks indicating conversion into less-toxic alkaloids. In the final formulation Swasanandam Gutika, aconitine was not detected, confirming significant detoxification and improved safety after purification.
Shodhita Vatsanabha showed fewer spots at both 254 nm and 366 nm, indicating denaturation/removal of toxic alkaloids, suggesting cow urine is a more effective purification medium than cow's milk.
Shodhana of Gunja seeds with lemon juice showed greater physico-chemical changes and more detectable components than raw and water-processed samples.

HPTLC showed altered chromatographic fingerprints after Shodhana, with fewer spots at both 254 nm and 366 nm and changes in Rf values, indicating denaturation/removal of certain constituents, thereby supporting detoxification of Gunja seeds.
HPTLC analysis confirmed a significant reduction in strychnine and brucine levels in purified seeds, with greater reduction observed after purification in Ardraka swarasa compared to Kanji.
HPTLC analysis showed that all Shodhana methods reduced strychnine and brucine levels compared to raw seeds, with the cow's urine followed by cow milk sequential method showing the maximum reduction.
HPTLC confirmed a 67.36% reduction in strychnine and a 46.97% reduction in brucine after Shodhana, demonstrating effective detoxification through the reduction of toxic alkaloids.

Shodhana significantly reduced the principal toxic alkaloids in Kuchala. Kanji Shodhana reduced strychnine by 59.20% and brucine by 71.27%, while cow's milk Shodhana reduced strychnine by 41.13% and brucine by 55.23%, confirming detoxification after Shodhana.
The HPTLC fingerprint changed after Shodhana, with the number of spots reducing from 5 (raw) to 3 (processed) at 254 nm, indicating alteration/removal of phytochemical constituents.
Purified Guggulu showed a statistically significant increase in Guggulsterone E and Z, indicating enhanced pharmacological potential after Shodhana.

HPTLC analysis of Karavira showed changes in chromatographic fingerprints (Rf shifts) after Shodhana, with spectral comparison indicating the transfer of cardiac glycoside-related constituents from the raw Karavira root to the processing media, supporting detoxification.
HPTLC analysis of Plumbago zeylanica after Shodhana showed an increase in plumbagin from 0.39% to 0.98%, indicating improved purity due to removal of water-soluble impurities.
No significant changes in SGOT, SGPT, ALP, LDH, urea, and creatinine at therapeutic doses, indicating absence of organ toxicity.

current_identifiers.result: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) confirmed Parada detoxification by demonstrating a significant reduction in toxic heavy metal impurities, with lead (Pb) decreasing from 6.34 to 0.90 ppm and tin (Sn) from 6.76 to 2.61 ppm after Shodhana.
AAS confirmed significant reduction of elemental impurities (Fe, Cu, Zn, Ag, Sn, Cd, Pb, and As) in mercury following Shodhana.
Shows very low levels of toxic metals (As 0.17%, Pb 0.03%), confirming purification during bhasma preparation.

Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy showed marked elemental changes after Shodhana–Marana, with copper content increasing by 65.85% (Method A) and 67.23% (Method B), sulfur by 8.87%/8.51%, and iron by 1.53%/1.76%, confirming chemical transformation of Tuttha during processing.

XRF analysis showed complete removal of lead (Pb) after Shodhana with Churnodaka and Kumari Swarasa (0.47% → undetectable), while tin (Sn) content increased from 99.08% in raw Vanga to 99.88% after Kumari Swarasa Shodhana, indicating enhanced purity.

Shodhita Tuttha showed larger zones of inhibition than crude Tuttha at all concentrations, confirming enhanced antimicrobial activity after Shodhana. It was effective against E. coli, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella typhi, Candida albicans and Trichophyton rubrum, while crude Tuttha showed limited activity mainly against Salmonella typhi.
Inflammatory changes (increased lymphocytes, and decreased neutrophils) seen with raw drug were reduced in Shodhita Dhattura, confirming decreased inflammatory toxicity.
Increase in Fe₂O₃ content and reduction in impurities (MgCO₃, CaCO₃, acid-insoluble matter) after processing confirmed purification and stabilization of iron in a therapeutically acceptable form.

Liver showed moderate fatty changes, diffuse and periportal necrosis, central vein congestion, and sinusoidal dilatation after high-dose treatment. Recovery animals exhibited almost normal liver architecture with only mild micro-fatty changes, indicating reversible hepatotoxic effects. Other vital organs showed normal cytoarchitecture.
Shodhita Manahshila produced a significant reduction in locomotor activity (P<0.001) in albino rats, indicating central nervous system depressant (sedative) effect.
pH shifted toward near-neutral after Shodhana and Marana (ZnCO₃: 8.73 to 7.73; ZnO: 6.04 to 5.9) confirming removal of impurities and improved biocompatibility.

current_identifiers.result: Significant reduction in symptoms with 96.66% decrease in white discharge, normalization of vaginal pH in 90% patients, marked reduction in pus and epithelial cells, increase in hemoglobin in 83.33% patients, overall maximum improvement in 56.67% cases, highly significant statistical improvement (P < 0.001), and no adverse effects observed confirming strong therapeutic efficacy and safety of the bhasma.
Total protein content decreased by 96.59–99.78% after Shodhana, with the greatest reduction in Kanji-treated samples, indicating marked reduction of the toxic protein (abrin)

Both groups receiving 500 mg/day Shilajit for 21 days showed a significant reduction in blood glucose levels in newly diagnosed hyperglycemic subjects, indicating effective hypoglycemic activity for both purification methods.

Shodhita Bhanga significantly reduced pain (84.1%), anxiety, and depression, improved quality of life, and showed no major adverse effects, dependency, or withdrawal symptoms. In contrast, unprocessed Cannabis is associated with habit formation and cognitive impairment, indicating that Shodhana improves its safety and therapeutic efficacy.

Shankha Bhasma purified with lemon juice showed significantly higher symptom resolution (66 to 71% vs. 27 to 31%, P < 0.005) and more heartburn-free days, confirming improved therapeutic efficacy after proper Shodhana.

THC ( Delta 9-tetrahydrocannabinol) content decreased by 26–85% after Shodhana, depending on the purification method, confirming significant removal of the narcotic principle. The greatest reduction (85%) was achieved by washing the leaves until free from turbidity followed by frying in ghee, indicating this as the most effective detoxification method.

Microscopic analysis showed that Shodhana reduced glandular trichomes (the major site of tetrahydrocannabinol, THC, accumulation), along with fragmented fibers, reduced cystoliths, and shrunken/distorted epidermal cells, indicating structural modifications associated with reduced psychoactive THC content and detoxification.

Purified Bhallataka exhibited greater thrombolytic activity (66.59% clot lysis) than raw Bhallataka (59.82%), demonstrating that Shodhana enhances the thrombolytic efficacy while producing a safer form of the drug.

ICP-MS analysis showed that Shodhana markedly reduced silver (5138 to 119.5 ppm), copper (2866.1 to 0.5324 ppm), and tin (0.371 to 0.3233 ppm) impurities, producing purified mercury with elemental composition closer to commercially available mercury.
Chemical analysis showed an increase in sulfur content from 89.39% to 97.14% after Shodhana, confirming improved purity of Sulphur.
Strychnine and brucine were detected in the post-Shodhana milk, confirming removal of the principal toxic alkaloids from Nux-vomica seeds during Shodhana.
